header.userPrompt:
# Spec: confirm a row into its matched existing expense, and see that expense first

## Problem
On the bank-statement Review page (`/bank-statements/:id`), the "Process ready"
bulk action already links a row to an existing unlinked expense when the matcher
returns `AutoLink` (receipt-backed expenses now win that match). But the per-row
UI does not expose this:

1. A row that will auto-link shows a static `↔ Link existing` chip that is not
   clickable, and the row's Match and Category cells show the import-rule / AI
   *suggestion*, not the matched expense's own merchant/category. The user cannot
   see which expense will be linked or its real merchant/category/notes, which
   usually differ from the suggestion.
2. The per-row primary button "Confirm" always opens the create-expense drawer
   (`BankRowCreateExpenseForm`), which lists unconfirmed *receipts* only. So when a
   row matches an existing expense, there is no per-row way to confirm *that link*;
   the only path to link an existing expense is buried in the "…" menu.

Goal: let the user confirm a single row into its matched existing expense (keeping
the link, same outcome as the bulk action), after seeing that expense's details.
The bulk "Process ready" flow stays exactly as it is.

## Relevant files (all under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/`)
- `BankStatementReviewRow.scala` — one table row. `Props.linksToExpense: Boolean`
  (line ~47) is the collapsed match flag; the `↔ Link existing` chip is a static
  `tintChip` (~line 175); `primaryActionFor` drives the primary button, and
  `PrimaryAction.ReviewExpense` renders "Confirm" → `RowAction.OpenExpenseForm`
  (~line 96-103). `matchCell` (~162) and `categoryCell` (~184) render the
  suggestion for not-yet-linked rows.
- `BankStatementReviewTable.scala` (~line 87) builds `linksToExpense` from
  `props.expenseMatchById.get(row.id)`, discarding the `AutoLink(expenseId)` id.
- `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` (~line 150-152) maps `RowAction.OpenExpenseForm`
  → `DrawerState.CreateExpense(rowId)` and `RowAction.OpenLinkPicker` →
  `DrawerState.LinkExpense(rowId)`. It holds the loaded expenses, categories, and
  merchants and builds `expenseMatchById`.
- `BankRowLinkPicker.scala` — the existing "Link to existing expense" drawer: loads
  all expenses via `getExpenses`, filters, and renders `date | amount | merchant |
  notes` rows each with a "Link" button that calls `linkRowToExpense`. This is the
  working link path; reuse it.
- `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` — `primaryActionFor` (~line 277), the
  `PrimaryAction` enum (~274), `RowInfo`. `ReconciliationMatcher.AutoLink(expenseId)`
  carries the matched expense id.
- `BankStatementRowActions.scala` — row-level API calls (`unlink`, `refreshRow`, …);
  `BankStatementReviewContent` already calls `linkRowToExpense` indirectly via the
  picker's `onSuccess`.

## Required behavior

### Thread the matched expense through to the row
Stop collapsing the match to a `Boolean`. Pass the matched expense id (from
`ReconciliationMatcher.AutoLink(expenseId)`) down to `BankStatementReviewRow`, and
resolve it to the already-loaded expense so the row can show its real data. Prefer
computing a small prepared value in the page/parent (matched expense id + its
merchant name + a category label built from its splits and the loaded categories,
"Multiple" when the splits span more than one category) and passing that to the
row, keeping the row component dumb. Do not add a new API call for this; the
expenses, categories and merchants are already loaded on the page.

### Gap 1 — show and inspect the matched expense
- When a not-yet-linked row has an `AutoLink` match, the Match cell shows the
  matched expense's merchant and the Category cell shows the matched expense's
  category label (not the rule/AI suggestion). Keep the `↔ Link existing` chip.
- Make the match affordance clickable: clicking it opens the link drawer for that
  row (see below) so the user can see the full expense (merchant, category, notes,
  amount, date, whether it has a receipt) before deciding. A static, unclickable
  chip is the current bug.

### Gap 2 — per-row "Confirm" links the matched expense
- When a row is ready (`PrimaryAction.ReviewExpense`) AND has an `AutoLink` match,
  "Confirm" opens the link drawer (`DrawerState.LinkExpense(rowId)`) instead of the
  create-expense drawer. Linking keeps the row linked to that existing expense
  (reuse `linkRowToExpense`), which inherits the expense's merchant/category/notes.
- When a ready row has no match, "Confirm" keeps opening the create-expense drawer
  as today.
- Keep the "…" menu entries ("Link to existing expense", "Create expense", etc.)
  as manual overrides, so the user can still create a new expense or pick a
  different one.

### Enhance `BankRowLinkPicker` to surface the match
- Accept an optional matched/suggested expense id. When present, show that expense
  first and prominently, with its full details: merchant, category (resolved from
  splits + categories, "Multiple" if several), notes, amount, date, and a receipt
  indicator if it has one. Give it a primary "Link this expense" button.
- Keep the existing filter and full list below as manual override, and make sure
  the matched expense is always shown even if it would fall outside the current
  `take(20)` slice.
- To render category names the picker needs the categories; pass them in from the
  page (already loaded) rather than fetching.

## Acceptance tests
Favor extracting pure logic into `BankStatementReviewLogic` and unit-testing it in
`BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`; add a thin component test only where it needs the
DOM.
1. `primaryActionFor` (or a new helper): a ready row with an `AutoLink` match
   resolves its "Confirm" to the link action; a ready row without a match resolves
   to the create action. Unignore / ignore-by-rule / refund cases unchanged.
2. The prepared-match helper: given an `AutoLink(expenseId)`, the loaded expenses,
   categories and merchants, it yields the matched expense's merchant name and the
   correct category label (single category name; "Multiple" for multi-split;
   empty/greyed when the expense or category is missing). A non-`AutoLink` match or
   a missing expense yields no prepared match.
3. Component test (BrowserRouter + jsdom, per docs/guide/testing.md): a row with a
   match renders the matched expense's merchant/category and a clickable `↔ Link
   existing`; clicking "Confirm" opens the link drawer (not the create drawer); the
   link drawer shows the matched expense first with a "Link this expense" button.
4. Existing bank-statement-review tests still pass unchanged, and bulk "Process
   ready" behavior is untouched.

## Repo conventions (must follow)
- Frontend only. No new API endpoints and no DB schema changes; reuse
  `linkRowToExpense`, `getExpenses`, and the loaded categories/merchants.
- Hook dependency lists go through `net.wiringbits.core.SafeHooks` with `String`
  keys (never a `UUID`, `Option`, collection or case class as a raw dep).
- Mutually-exclusive UI state is one ADT in a single `useState`, not parallel
  flags; derive state from its previous value with the functional updater
  (`set(_ + x)`), never `set(closureValue + x)`.
- Component tests use `BrowserRouter` + jsdom; `null.asInstanceOf[API]` only when
  the component never calls `ctx.api`; object-level `val`s hold only plain JS
  literals; React elements reused in a render tree use `def`, not `val`.
- Comments explain intent, not the change history.
- Pre-push sequence, in this exact order:
  1. `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
  2. `git add` new/changed files
  3. `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`, then re-stage reformatted files
  4. `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` (foreground) must exit 0
  5. push
- The repo is public: keep commit messages and the PR description free of any PII
  (account numbers, real merchant names, amounts) and free of Claude session links.
- Surgical changes, match existing style, keep the bulk flow and the server
  untouched.

resultJson.description:
On the bank-statement Review page (`/bank-statements/:id`), a ready debit row whose `ReconciliationMatcher` result is `AutoLink(expenseId)` gets linked to that existing expense by the bulk "Process ready" action. The per-row UI doesn't show this. The row's Match and Category cells show the rule/AI suggestion instead of the matched expense's own merchant and category. The `↔ Link existing` chip is static. The row's "Confirm" button always opens the create-expense drawer, so the only per-row way to link is the "…" menu, and that link picker never highlights the matched expense.

This epic is frontend only. The page already holds `expenseMatchById` plus the loaded expenses, categories and merchants. Instead of collapsing the match to a `Boolean`, it resolves the match into a small prepared value (expense id, merchant name, category label with "Multiple" for multi-split) and passes that down to the dumb, memoized row. The row shows that expense's merchant and category, makes the `↔ Link existing` chip clickable, and routes "Confirm" for a matched ready row to the existing link drawer (`DrawerState.LinkExpense`). Unmatched ready rows still open the create form.

`BankRowLinkPicker` gets an optional matched expense id and the page's categories. It shows the matched expense first with its full details (merchant, category, notes, amount, date, receipt indicator) and a primary "Link this expense" button. The existing filter and list stay below it as a manual override. Linking still goes through `linkRowToExpense`. Bulk "Process ready", the server, the API and the DB are not touched.

tasks.title: Pure logic: prepared expense match, expense category label, ConfirmLink primary action, picker list split
tasks.description:
Only `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` and `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec.scala` change in this task.

1. Add `def expenseCategory(expense: GetExpenses.Response.Expense, categories: List[GetCategories.Response.Category]): LinkedCategory`, reusing the existing `LinkedCategory` enum. Take the distinct `splits.map(_.categoryId)`: none → `Unknown`; exactly one → `Named(name)` if it is in `categories`, else `Unknown`; more than one → `Multiple`.
2. Add `final case class MatchedExpense(expenseId: UUID, merchantName: Option[String], category: LinkedCategory)` and `def matchedExpense(proposed: Option[ReconciliationMatcher.ProposedAction], expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense], categories: ..., merchants: List[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant]): Option[MatchedExpense]`.
   - Return Some only for `Some(AutoLink(id))` where `id` is in `expenses`.
   - Merchant name: `expense.merchantName`, falling back to looking up `expense.merchantId` in `merchants`.
   - Category: `expenseCategory(expense, categories)`.
   - Also add `def matchedExpenses(expenseMatchById: Map[UUID, ProposedAction], expenses, categories, merchants): Map[UUID, MatchedExpense]` for the page to memoize.
3. Extend `PrimaryAction` with a new case `ConfirmLink`. Add a trailing defaulted parameter: `primaryActionFor(row, isReady, verdict, hasExpenseMatch: Boolean = false)`. The ready-debit branch returns `ConfirmLink` when `hasExpenseMatch`, else `ReviewExpense`. Refund, ignore-by-rule, unignore and linked precedence stay unchanged, and existing call sites and tests compile untouched. Update the enum/def scaladoc to explain the intent.
4. Add `def linkPickerEntries(expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense], filter: String, matchedId: Option[UUID]): (Option[GetExpenses.Response.Expense], List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense])`.
   - Pull the matched expense out unconditionally, regardless of the filter or the 20-item cap.
   - Apply the picker's existing filter predicate (date, amount, merchantName, notes, lowercase contains) to the rest, exclude the matched one, and `take(20)`.
   - Move the predicate here from `BankRowLinkPicker`, but don't touch the picker yet; that is a later task.
5. Add tests to `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`:
   - `primaryActionFor`: ready debit with a match → `ConfirmLink`; without a match → `ReviewExpense`; Ignore verdict, ready credit, ignored and linked rows are unchanged even with `hasExpenseMatch = true`.
   - `matchedExpense`: single-category label; "Multiple" for multi-split; `Unknown` when the category is missing or there are no splits; merchant-name fallback through `merchants`; None for `NeedsReview`, `CreateNew`, `None` and a missing expense.
   - `linkPickerEntries`: matched first even when outside the first 20 or filtered out; not duplicated; filter works.

Verify with `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"`.

tasks.title: Thread the matched expense to the row: show its merchant and category, clickable Link existing chip, Confirm opens the link drawer
tasks.description:
Depends on the logic task.

- **`BankStatementReviewContent.scala`:** memoize `matchedExpenseById = SafeHooks.useMemo(rowsKey, rowInfoKey, expensesKey, merchantsKey, categoriesKey)(() => matchedExpenses(expenseMatchById, expenseList, categoryList, merchantList))`. Use only String keys. Pass it to the table. `onRowAction` needs no change, because Confirm will emit the existing `RowAction.OpenLinkPicker`.
- **`BankStatementReviewTable.scala`:** replace the `expenseMatchById` prop with `matchedExpenseById: Map[UUID, MatchedExpense]`; it was only used for `linksToExpense`. Pass `matchedExpense = props.matchedExpenseById.get(row.id)` to each row.
- **`BankStatementReviewRow.scala`:** replace `linksToExpense: Boolean` with `matchedExpense: Option[MatchedExpense]`. Rows are `React.memo`'d on case-class equality, and `MatchedExpense` is a case class, so that still works.
  - Call `primaryActionFor(row, info.isReady, info.verdict, hasExpenseMatch = props.matchedExpense.isDefined)`. The new `PrimaryAction.ConfirmLink` case renders the same contained "Confirm" button as `ReviewExpense`, but its onClick is `act(RowAction.OpenLinkPicker)`.
  - In `matchCell`, for not-linked, non-Ignore rows with a match, the merchant chip shows `matchedExpense.merchantName` (fall back to `dash` when it is None) instead of `info.merchantName`. Keep the `↔ Link existing` chip, but make it clickable: MUI Chip `.clickable(true).onClick(_ => act(RowAction.OpenLinkPicker))`. Build a separate def rather than changing `tintChip`'s signature for all callers.
  - In `categoryCell`, for not-linked, non-Ignore rows with a match, render `matchedExpense.category` the same way as the linked branch: Named → chip, Multiple → "Multiple" chip, Unknown → `dash`. Do not show the AI tag.
  - Update the cell comments to describe the intent.
- **`BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala`:** change only the `props` helper parameter, from `linksToExpense: Boolean` to `matchedExpense: Option[MatchedExpense] = None`. Adapt the one existing Link-existing test's arguments; its assertions stay. Add tests:
  - A matched row shows the expense's merchant in td(5) and its category in td(4), not the suggestion's "Groceries".
  - Clicking the `↔ Link existing` chip reports `OpenLinkPicker`.
  - Clicking "Confirm" on a matched ready row reports `OpenLinkPicker`, not `OpenExpenseForm`.
  - Multi-split shows "Multiple".
  - The existing "Confirm → OpenExpenseForm" test still passes for an unmatched row.

Verify with `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewRowSpec *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"`, then `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Link picker surfaces the matched expense first with full details and "Link this expense"
tasks.description:
Depends on the logic task. Can be done before or after the row task.

- **`BankRowLinkPicker.Props`:** add `matchedExpenseId: Option[UUID]` and `categories: List[GetCategories.Response.Category]`.
  - Keep fetching with `getExpenses` as today.
  - Use `BankStatementReviewLogic.linkPickerEntries(expenses, filter, props.matchedExpenseId)` in place of the inline filter and `take(20)`.
  - When the matched expense is present, render it above the filter in a highlighted box (for example a `mui.Box` with a `var(--lc-tint)` background and padding), with a caption such as "Matched expense". Show:
    - merchant (`merchantName`, or "-")
    - category, from `expenseCategory(e, props.categories)`: Named → name, Multiple → "Multiple", Unknown → "—"
    - notes, if any
    - amount
    - date
    - "🧾 Receipt" when `receiptIds.nonEmpty`
    - a contained primary `Button` "Link this expense" → `handleLink(e.id)`
  - Below the matched expense, keep the existing filter and the `date | amount | merchant | notes` + "Link" rows as the manual override.
  - Use `def` for any helper that returns a ReactElement, and use `.withKey` on mapped rows.
- **`BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala`:** add a prop `expenseMatchById: Map[UUID, ReconciliationMatcher.ProposedAction]` (or `matchedExpenseById: Map[UUID, MatchedExpense]`; pick one and stay consistent). In the `LinkExpense` branch, pass `matchedExpenseId` for `row.id` (the id of an AutoLink match) and `categories = props.categories`.
- **`BankStatementReviewContent.scala`:** pass that map into `BankStatementReviewDrawer.Props`.
- **New spec, `web/src/test/scala/.../bankstatementreview/BankRowLinkPickerSpec.scala`**, using `ReactTestDom` and `BrowserRouter`. The picker calls `ctx.api.client` in an effect, so `null.asInstanceOf[API]` is not allowed here.
  - Build `AppContext(api = API(stubClient, null.asInstanceOf[StorageService], ""), …)`. Copy the `testCtx` shape from `ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec`, using `ExecutionContext.parasitic` for both the stub and `executionContext`.
  - `stubClient` extends `ApiClient(ApiClient.Config("http://localhost"))(using ExecutionContext.parasitic, SttpBackendStub.asynchronousFuture)`, overriding `getExpenses` (and `linkRowToExpense`, recording calls). Use the `StubClient` in `BankStatementRowActionsSpec` as the template. Use neutral fake merchant names and amounts.
  - Tests: (a) the matched expense renders first with its merchant, category, notes and a "Link this expense" button, even when it is past the first 20 expenses; (b) clicking "Link this expense" calls `linkRowToExpense` with that id, then `onSuccess(id)`; (c) with no `matchedExpenseId`, only the list renders, as before.
  - Add a comment stating the runtime failure the DOM test guards against: element reuse or keying in the mixed matched-plus-list render, and the async load path. RULE-TE-010 requires it.

Verify with `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankRowLinkPickerSpec *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"`, then `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- `web/` is a Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5 frontend. All work is in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/` plus the tests mirrored under `web/src/test/scala/...`. There are no server, API (`lib/api/shared`) or DB changes.
- `ReconciliationMatcher` is at `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala`: `sealed trait ProposedAction`, `case class AutoLink(expenseId: UUID)`, `NeedsReview(ids)`, `CreateNew`.

KEY FILES
- `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` holds the pure logic (no React).
  - `RowInfo(verdict, resolved, refund, prefillMerchantId, isReady, merchantName, categoryName, linkedMerchantName, linkedCategory)`.
  - `enum LinkedCategory { Named(name), Multiple, Unknown }`; reuse it for the matched expense's category label.
  - `enum PrimaryAction { Linked, Unignore, IgnoreByRule, ReviewExpense, ReviewRefund, CreateRefund, CreateExpense }`.
  - `primaryActionFor(row, isReady, verdict)` (~l.277).
  - `enum DrawerState { Closed, CreateExpense(rowId), CreateRefund, LinkExpense(rowId), CreateRule }` with `closing(form)`.
  - `expenseMatches(rows, rowInfoById, unlinkedByDate): Map[UUID, ProposedAction]`.
  - `bulkRowDecision`: bulk logic, do NOT change.
- `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` is the page body.
  - It reads `support` (`merchantList`, `categoryList`, `ruleList`, `expenseList` = unlinked candidate expenses in the statement window).
  - It memoizes with `SafeHooks.useMemo(stringKeys*)(() => …)`; existing keys: `rowsKey`, `merchantsKey`, `categoriesKey`, `expensesKey`, `rowInfoKey` (all `.toString` of lists).
  - It builds `expenseMatchById`.
  - `onRowAction` maps `RowAction.OpenExpenseForm` → `DrawerState.CreateExpense` and `OpenLinkPicker` → `DrawerState.LinkExpense`. It is a stable `SafeHooks.useCallback` keyed on a String.
  - `onExpenseLinked` already patches the row, closes the drawer and calls `refreshRow`.
  - It passes `expenseMatchById` to `BankStatementBulkRuns.handleBulkImport`; leave that as is.
- `BankStatementReviewTable.scala` maps rows to `BankStatementReviewRow(...).withKey(row.id.toString)`. Today it collapses `expenseMatchById.get(row.id)` to `linksToExpense: Boolean` (l.87).
- `BankStatementReviewRow.scala` is a `React.memo` component compared with case-class equality (`prev == next`), so every prop must be a value with structural equality and callbacks must be stable.
  - Helpers: `tintChip(lbl, textColor)`, `dash`, `suggestingOrDash`, `smallTextButton`, `act(action)`.
  - Cells: `matchCell` (l.162) and `categoryCell` (l.184). The column order puts Category at td(4) and Match at td(5).
  - The "Confirm" button is in the `PrimaryAction.ReviewExpense` branch (l.96).
- `BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala` holds the per-form drawer. It already has `categories` and `merchants` in Props. Its `LinkExpense` branch builds `BankRowLinkPicker.Props(stmtId, rowId, ctx, onSuccess, onCancel)`.
- `BankRowLinkPicker.scala` fetches `ctx.api.client.getExpenses` (all expenses) in `SafeHooks.useEffect()`. It filters inline and renders `filtered.take(20)` rows, `date | amount | merchant | notes` + "Link". `handleLink(expenseId)` calls `client.linkRowToExpense(bankStatementId, rowId, LinkRowToExpense.Request(expenseId))` and then `props.onSuccess(expenseId)`.
- Model `GetExpenses.Response.Expense(id, amount: BigDecimal, date: LocalDate, time, merchantId: Option[UUID], merchantName: Option[String], notes: Option[String], splits: List[Split(id, categoryId, amount)], createdAt, receiptIds: List[UUID] = Nil, rowIds: List[UUID] = Nil)` lives in `lib/api/shared/.../expenses/GetExpenses.scala`.
- `GetCategories.Response.Category` has `id` and `name`. `GetMerchants.Response.Merchant` has `id`, `name` and `categoryId: Option[UUID]`.

TESTS
- `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` uses AnyWordSpec + `must` matchers and a `sampleRow()` helper; the existing `primaryActionFor` block is at ~l.243. `should` subjects name the method only, never the class (RULE-TE-001).
- `BankStatementReviewRowSpec` uses `ReactTestDom` (gives `container`, `act`, `render`) with `BrowserRouter(basename = "")`. Its `props(...)` helper has a `linksToExpense` param that must be renamed when the Row prop changes. Keep the existing assertions unchanged. `clickButton(label)` expects exactly one matching button.
- Fixtures to copy:
  - Stub `ApiClient`: `BankStatementRowActionsSpec` `StubClient` (extends `ApiClient(ApiClient.Config("http://localhost"))(using ExecutionContext.parasitic, SttpBackendStub.asynchronousFuture)`, overriding methods).
  - `AppContext`: `ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec.testCtx()`. `AppContext(api, $auth, $lang, $darkMode, contactEmail, contactPhone, executionContext)`; `API(client: ApiClient, storage: StorageService, serverUrl: String)`.
- `null.asInstanceOf[API]` is only allowed when the component never touches `ctx.api`. The picker does, so it needs a real `API` wrapping a stub client.
- Targeted runs only: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *XSpec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. `CI=true` turns warnings into errors (unused imports or params fail). Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, so yarn install fails). Do not run the full `sbt test`.

CONVENTIONS
- Hook deps go only through `net.wiringbits.core.SafeHooks` with String keys; never use a UUID, Option, collection or case class as a raw dep.
- Mutually exclusive UI state is one ADT in one `useState` (the drawer already uses `DrawerState`). Use functional updaters (`set(_ + x)`).
- Object-level `val`s may hold only plain JS literals or CSS objects (like `secondaryStyling`), never ReactElement or KeyAddingStage. React elements reused in a tree must be `def`. Mapped elements need `.withKey`.
- Ascribe MUI builders with `(... .build: ReactElement)` as the existing code does. Chip supports `.clickable(true)` and `.onClick(...)`.
- Comments explain intent, not change history. Make surgical changes and match the existing style.
- Keep the "…" menu items (Link to existing expense, Create rule, Ignore) as manual overrides.
- Fixtures and commits use no real merchant names or amounts; the repo is public.

NON-OBVIOUS
- `expenseMatchById` only contains ready, non-Ignore debit rows, so a match implies the row is ready. A matched expense is always in `expenseList`, which is unlinked, windowed, and kept current via `refreshExpenses`.
- The picker's `getExpenses` returns all expenses, including linked ones, so the matched one will be in it. It must still appear first even past `take(20)`.
- The server only reports `row.expenseCategoryId` for single-split linked expenses. For a matched (not yet linked) expense, compute the category from its splits instead.
- `primaryActionFor` has callers in `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` at l.250-278, 407 and 442. A defaulted new parameter keeps them unchanged.

resultJson.title: Let a bank statement row's Confirm link its matched existing expense
resultJson.body:
On the bank statement Review page, a ready row that matches an existing expense (`AutoLink`) is linked to it by bulk "Process ready". Until now the row itself didn't show that. This PR adds the same outcome to the row, and you can see the expense before you confirm. Frontend only. The bulk flow, server and API are unchanged.

- **Row shows the matched expense.** The page resolves each `AutoLink` match into a `MatchedExpense` (expense id, merchant name, category label) using the expenses, categories and merchants it has already loaded. The label is "Multiple" when the splits span more than one category. For a matched row, the Match and Category cells show the expense's own merchant and category instead of the rule/AI suggestion.
- **Confirm links instead of creating.** On a ready, matched debit row, "Confirm" (new `PrimaryAction.ConfirmLink`) opens the link drawer instead of the create-expense form. Ready rows with no match work as before. The `↔ Link existing` chip can now be clicked and opens the same drawer.
- **Link picker shows the match first.** `BankRowLinkPicker` now receives the matched expense id and the categories. It shows that expense at the top with merchant, category, notes, amount, date, a receipt indicator and a "Link this expense" button. It stays at the top even if the filter would hide it or it falls outside the 20-item limit. The filter and full list are still below it for picking a different expense. Linking still goes through `linkRowToExpense`.
- **New "Create new expense" menu item.** The "…" menu of an open debit row now has this item, so you can still create a new expense when Confirm would link the match.

For reviewers: `primaryActionFor` now takes a required `matchedExpense` argument, so the existing call sites and tests were updated to pass `None`. The filter logic moved from the picker into `BankStatementReviewLogic.linkPickerEntries`. New tests cover the logic, the row and the picker (`BankRowLinkPickerSpec`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
